_meta.what_this_is: An evaluation whose GOLD LABELS are themselves wrong a fraction k of the time (label noise). A model is scored by how often it AGREES with the label -- but when the label is wrong, a correct model disagrees with it and loses a point it deserved. So measured accuracy is not the model true accuracy: measured = a*(1-k) + (1-a)*k, which is capped at 1-k. A perfect model cannot score above 1-k, and improvements near that ceiling are partly masked because each real gain moves the measured score by less than itself.
_meta.data_is: A FIXTURE. The label noise rate and the models true accuracies are hand-authored so the ceiling (0.90) is clear: a perfect model scores exactly 0.90, and the gap between models measures smaller than it truly is. Every measured accuracy is computed in labelnoise.py under the standard independent-error model.
_meta.format: label_noise: fraction of gold labels that are wrong; models: {name: true_accuracy}.
